hero.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to strike Iran as tensions escalate
hero.body:
President Trump appealed to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from retaliating against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomatic efforts, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the conversation. The call came as the Israeli military confirmed it had struck targets inside Iran in response to an Iranian missile attack.

Trump told reporters before the call that he intended to ask Netanyahu not to respond to Iran's strike, which Tehran said was motivated by an earlier Israeli attack on Beirut. The exchange of strikes between the two nations risks escalating tensions across the entire Middle East region and could undermine ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran.

The Trump administration did not authorize the initial Israeli strike in Beirut, according to a senior U.S. official. Despite Trump's appeal for restraint, Israel proceeded with its retaliatory strikes on Iranian military targets. The sequence of events marks a significant escalation in the months-long conflict between Israel and Iran.

Trump's attempt to limit Israel's military response reflects his administration's broader strategy to prevent escalating Israel-Iran tensions from derailing diplomatic channels with Tehran. The president has focused on maintaining negotiations while managing regional conflicts and supporting American allies in the area.

When asked about whether the military actions contradicted his 2024 campaign promise of avoiding new wars, Trump dismissed the suggestion. He argued that his approach does not betray his "no new wars" message as he campaigned for the White House.

The confrontation between Israel and Iran has created significant diplomatic challenges for the administration. Saturday's emergency UN Security Council meeting grew contentious after Secretary General António Guterres condemned both the U.S.-Israeli strikes and Iran's retaliatory attacks as violations of international law.

The timing of events placed particular focus on the Trump administration's international engagement. The first lady presided over a UN Security Council meeting on Monday focused on children, technology, and education in conflict zones. Melania Trump emphasized education's role in preventing conflict and called for protecting children's access to learning. The session came just days after the escalated strikes between Israel and Iran.

Iran's UN ambassador criticized the timing as hypocritical, noting that Washington was convening a meeting on child protection while simultaneously launching airstrikes on Iranian cities. Iranian state media reported that strikes had killed at least 165 people at a girls' school in southern Iran, though the Israeli military said it was unaware of strikes in that area, and the U.S. military said it was investigating the reports.

The crisis has tested Trump's ability to balance multiple diplomatic objectives including supporting Israel, pursuing negotiations with Iran, and maintaining broader regional stability. The outcome of these efforts remains uncertain as both nations have demonstrated willingness to conduct military operations despite presidential appeals for restraint.

cards.headline: Israel and Iran Exchange Strikes in Retaliatory Attacks
cards.teaser: Israel and Iran traded fire in retaliatory strikes that risk escalating conflict across the Middle East.
cards.body:
Israel and Iran traded fire early Monday in a series of retaliatory strikes. The exchange began with Iran launching a missile barrage at Israel, followed by Israeli counterattacks. The strikes threatened to pull the wider Middle East into regional conflict.

The escalation involved multiple parties in the region. Israel also conducted retaliatory attacks against Hezbollah in Beirut's suburbs after the militant group struck Israeli military targets with fighter drones, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. The cycle of attacks raised concerns about broader warfare spreading across the region.

cards.headline: At Least 12 People Shot at Street Festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
Police are continuing their search for at least two gunmen who opened fire at the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday evening, wounding 12 people. Festival organizers have cancelled Sunday's planned events as the investigation enters its second day.

The shooting erupted just after 5:30 p.m. near the Old West End festival, an annual community gathering featuring live music and architectural home tours. Toledo Police Deputy Chief Joseph Heffernan said the shooters were "probably shooting at each other" when the gunfire broke out. Several hundred people were attending the festival at the time.

Two victims are reported to be in critical condition. The ages of those shot ranged from 14 to 61 years old, with most in their early 20s. The fire chief reported that it was difficult to transport victims to area hospitals because closed roads and traffic from people leaving the festival hampered emergency response efforts.

With no suspects yet in custody, law enforcement officials have asked festival attendees to come forward with any photos or videos from their phones that might provide leads. Police noted that extra officers had been assigned to the festival, and a large number of off-duty officers were working the event itself.

Heffernan expressed frustration about the violence disrupting a longstanding community tradition. "It's just a shame when a few people, for whatever reasons going through their head, decide to disrupt something that has been a beloved community event for many, many, many years," he said.

Festival organizers released a statement expressing heartbreak over the incident. "Too often we turn on the news and learn of a celebration somewhere that turns into a tragedy. Now, that news comes from our own neighborhood," the statement read. After consulting with Toledo civic and police authorities, organizers determined that continuing the festival would not be "compassionate, responsible or possible."

The incident drew responses from state officials. Ohio Governor Mike DeWine said in a statement, "Summer festivals should be safe spaces for families to spend time together without fear of violence." State Senator Jon Husted called the violence "senseless" and thanked law enforcement for acting quickly and working to locate suspects.

This shooting is among more than 170 mass shooting incidents that have occurred in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines mass shootings as incidents in which four or more victims are wounded or killed. The Toledo incident reflects the ongoing challenge of gun violence at public gatherings across the country.

cards.headline: Earthquake in southern Philippines kills at least 15
cards.teaser: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the southern Philippines, killing at least 15 people and injuring 129.
cards.body:
A powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the southern Philippines early Monday, collapsing buildings and killing at least 15 people, with 129 others injured. The quake was centered at sea and caused widespread damage across the region, knocking out power in affected areas.

Authorities issued tsunami warnings, and officials reported 1-meter waves following the earthquake. Residents were warned to avoid damaged buildings and structures due to the risk of aftershocks as rescue operations continued.

cards.headline: Airlines face $100 billion fuel cost increase as Iran conflict disrupts oil supplies
cards.teaser: Global airlines slashed profit forecasts after projecting an extra $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year due to energy disruptions from the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Airlines are bracing for an additional $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year as oil prices surge following escalating tensions between Iran and Israel. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil supplies, has become effectively unusable, constraining available fuel and driving up prices.

The industry has already begun cutting profit forecasts for 2026. Carriers warn that higher ticket prices appear unavoidable as they grapple with the fuel cost shock. The International Air Transport Association addressed the crisis at its 82nd annual meeting, where leaders discussed the financial implications for operations and passenger fares.

cards.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets for Gulf ally reconstruction
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect Iranian assets to help Gulf allies rebuild from war damage.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department is planning to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in the rebuilding process resulting from Iranian damage from the war. A source aware of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's thinking confirmed the plan to CBS News.

The move comes as the U.S. attempts to manage escalating tensions between Israel and Iran while supporting regional partners. The use of Iranian assets represents one tool in the administration's broader strategy to address the conflict's regional impact.

cards.headline: Trump defends Iran military action against campaign promise criticism
cards.teaser: The president rejected claims that military operations involving Iran contradict his 'no new wars' pledge.
cards.body:
President Trump is rejecting claims that military action involving Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge to avoid new wars. Trump repeatedly promised during his presidential campaign to steer clear of new military conflicts abroad.

The administration is now addressing questions about how current operations in the region align with those campaign commitments as U.S. involvement continues to develop.

cards.headline: Asian tech stocks drop after Middle East attacks
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan fell after renewed attacks in the Middle East ended a recent rally in technology stocks.
cards.body:
Stock markets in South Korea and Japan declined on Monday as geopolitical tensions escalated following renewed military strikes between Iran and Israel. The selloff reversed recent gains, with technology stocks leading the retreat after rallying in prior weeks.

Investor concerns about regional stability prompted the market pullback, as geopolitical risks returned to the center of attention in Asian trading.

cards.headline: Peru presidential runoff remains too close to call
cards.teaser: A leftist candidate and a right-wing rival are in a neck-and-neck race after Peru's presidential runoff election.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential runoff pitted leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez against right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori, the daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori. Sánchez finished second in April's first round with 12% of the vote, while Fujimori garnered 17%, setting up a polarized left-right contest for the presidency.

The election took place amid deep instability, with Peru having cycled through nine presidents in a decade. Voters prioritized tackling rising crime and corruption, alongside demands for political stability that would allow the next leader to address inequality and insecurity.

cards.headline: Israel struck Beirut suburb after Hezbollah attack
cards.teaser: Israeli forces bombed Beirut's outskirts following a Hezbollah attack, days after a U.S.-brokered truce.
cards.body:
Israel launched retaliatory strikes on Beirut's suburbs following a Hezbollah attack using fighter drones against Israeli military targets, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. The operation marks an escalation in fighting between the two sides.

The strikes come just days after a U.S.-brokered cease-fire was established, resuming hostilities despite recent diplomatic efforts. The Israeli military also reported discovering a Hezbollah tunnel complex beneath Beaufort during operations in the region.

cards.headline: Five injured in stabbing at Penn Station in New York
cards.teaser: A stabbing at Penn Station in New York City left five people injured as the city increased security ahead of a presidential visit.
cards.body:
Five people were injured in a stabbing at Penn Station in New York City. The incident occurred as the city was heightening security measures in preparation for President Trump's visit to watch the NBA finals on Monday.

Authorities responded to the scene at the busy transit hub, where the city had already increased its police presence ahead of the planned presidential visit.

cards.headline: Spain records highest-ever April tourist numbers
cards.teaser: Spain welcomed 9.1 million international visitors in April, the most ever recorded for that month.
cards.body:
Spain received 9.1 million international visitors in April, setting a new record for that month. The surge came as tourists avoided the Middle East due to ongoing regional conflicts.

The tourism boost represents a shift in travel patterns as security concerns in other regions drove visitors to European destinations. Spain has benefited from its reputation as a stable alternative as Middle East tensions have escalated.

cards.headline: Extreme heat drives search for shade in Pakistan district
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District in Pakistan face temperatures reaching 125 degrees as the area contends with seasonal extremes.
cards.body:
People in Dadu District, Pakistan, are searching for shade as temperatures climb to 125 degrees. The region faces extreme weather challenges throughout the year, including sandstorms, drought, and flooding.

The district's residents struggle with each season bringing a new environmental hardship. The current heat wave adds to the area's ongoing vulnerability to climate extremes that affect daily life and survival.

cards.headline: Six People Stabbed at Penn Station in Manhattan
cards.teaser: A knife attack at Penn Station in New York City left six people injured.
cards.body:
Five people were injured in a stabbing attack at Penn Station in Manhattan, according to the New York City Fire Department. Police arrested a suspect in connection with the incident at the major transit hub.

The stabbing occurred as the city enhanced security measures ahead of President Trump's visit on Monday to attend the NBA finals.

cards.headline: Three Dead in Apparent Murder-Suicide in Canoga Park
cards.teaser: Twin 10-year-old boys and a man were found dead in a shooting police are investigating as a murder-suicide.
cards.body:
A man and twin 10-year-old boys died in an apparent murder-suicide shooting in Canoga Park, Los Angeles, according to police. The Los Angeles Police Department is investigating the deaths as a suspected murder-suicide.

Authorities discovered the three bodies at a residence in the Canoga Park neighborhood. Multiple local news outlets reported on the incident, which occurred in the San Fernando Valley area of Los Angeles.

cards.headline: Trump Ends NBC Interview After Clash Over Election Claims
cards.teaser: Former President Donald Trump walked out of an interview with NBC's Meet the Press after being challenged on election fraud claims.
cards.body:
Donald Trump walked out of an NBC News interview with moderator Kristen Welker after being repeatedly challenged on his claims that the 2020 presidential election and California gubernatorial races were rigged. The confrontation occurred during a Friday interview in Wisconsin that aired on Sunday.

The exchange also covered questions about compensation for those charged in the January 6 insurrection. Trump has made numerous false claims about election fraud following previous electoral losses.

cards.headline: Senate Candidate Graham Platner Holds Rally in Maine Amid Controversy
cards.teaser: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner received support from a friendly crowd after a week focused on damage control over allegations.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a former Marine-turned-oyster farmer, held a town hall in Portland where he received support from Maine voters. This came after a difficult week addressing allegations about his past conduct, including sexually explicit messages sent to women while married and a Nazi-themed tattoo.

Democratic congressman Ro Khanna offered qualified support for Platner's Senate bid against Republican Susan Collins, describing his actions as "misogynistic, shameful, and wrong." Some Maine Democrats said they are backing Platner reluctantly despite the controversy, with the candidate working to rebuild support within his party.

cards.headline: 7.8 Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Southern Philippines
cards.teaser: A major earthquake centered at sea shook the southern Philippines, causing damage and triggering tsunami waves.
cards.body:
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake centered at sea shook southern Philippines early Monday, causing widespread damage and knocking out power across affected areas. The seismic event triggered 1-meter tsunami waves, according to officials.

The earthquake collapsed multiple buildings and killed at least 15 people. Authorities urged residents to avoid damaged structures and buildings due to the risk of aftershocks while rescue operations continued in affected areas.

cards.headline: Israel and Iran Exchange Strikes in Retaliatory Attacks
cards.teaser: Israel and Iran traded fire in retaliatory strikes that risk escalating conflict across the Middle East.
cards.body:
Israel and Iran traded fire early Monday in a series of retaliatory strikes. The exchange began with Iran launching a missile barrage at Israel, followed by Israeli counterattacks. The strikes threatened to pull the wider Middle East into regional conflict.

The escalation involved multiple parties in the region. Israel also conducted retaliatory attacks against Hezbollah in Beirut's suburbs after the militant group struck Israeli military targets with fighter drones, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. The cycle of attacks raised concerns about broader warfare spreading across the region.

hero.headline: Asian stocks plunge as tech selloff intensifies and Middle East tensions spike oil prices
hero.body:
Asian stock markets dropped sharply after technology stocks suffered their worst selloff in months, driven by a combination of profit-taking following weeks of gains and renewed military strikes between Iran and Israel that sent oil prices surging.

South Korea's Kospi index plunged 7 percent, leading regional losses as investors unwound positions in technology stocks that had rallied to record highs in recent weeks. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained more than 5 percent, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 jumped 2.55 percent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng was up 3.1 percent, while China's CSI 300 index gained 3.2 percent. The selloff followed a sharp decline on Wall Street, where Big Tech stocks led broader market losses in their worst single-day performance in months.

The downturn marked a sudden reversal for tech stocks that had been buoying markets with a prolonged rally driven by artificial intelligence investments. The retreat highlighted concerns about the sustainability of recent gains built on expectations for AI-related earnings growth.

Oil prices jumped more than 3 percent after Iran and Israel exchanged military strikes, raising concerns about the stability of Middle East relations and the potential impact on global energy supplies. Crude prices climbed more than $3 per barrel as traders assessed the potential for further conflict and disruptions to shipping through critical waterways.

The dual pressures of the technology sector retreat and geopolitical tensions created widespread uncertainty across Asian trading floors. Investors shifted away from riskier assets as concerns mounted about both the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom that had driven recent gains and the economic impact of potential energy disruptions.

Wall Street rallied strongly following the market turmoil, with the S&P 500 advancing 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq Composite climbing 2.8 percent. The Dow Jones industrial average gained more than 1,300 points, or 2.9 percent. Travel and leisure stocks surged across global markets on the ceasefire developments, while oil company shares tumbled as crude prices fell from earlier highs.

European stock markets also rallied strongly, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 index gaining 3.7 percent, its biggest one-day rise in a year. The FTSE 100 in London closed up 2.5 percent at its highest end-of-day level since the start of the conflict.

Analysts noted that markets would continue monitoring the fragile truce between the parties. According to Kathleen Brooks, a research director at trading platform XTB, a complete breakdown of the ceasefire could send oil prices surging back above $110 per barrel for Brent crude, potentially causing stocks and bonds to slump.

The market turbulence highlighted the fragility of recent gains in technology stocks and the ongoing vulnerability of global markets to Middle East instability, with trading activity suggesting investors were reassessing positions while preparing for potential volatility from both sectors.

cards.headline: Airlines face $100 billion fuel cost increase as Iran conflict disrupts oil supplies
cards.teaser: Global airlines slashed profit forecasts after projecting an extra $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year due to energy disruptions from the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Airlines are bracing for an additional $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year as oil prices surge following escalating tensions between Iran and Israel. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil supplies, has become effectively unusable, constraining available fuel and driving up prices.

The industry has already begun cutting profit forecasts for 2026. Carriers warn that higher ticket prices appear unavoidable as they grapple with the fuel cost shock. The International Air Transport Association addressed the crisis at its 82nd annual meeting, where leaders discussed the financial implications for operations and passenger fares.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus increases oil output by 188,000 barrels per day as Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted
cards.teaser: The oil cartel raised production targets, but the increase appears largely symbolic given vast amounts of oil remain stranded by the Strait of Hormuz shutdown.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced it will boost oil production by 188,000 barrels per day as the ceasefire in Iran remains elusive. The cartel's decision comes as the conflict continues to disrupt global energy markets and shipping routes through the strategic waterway.

The production increase is considered largely symbolic given the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz has stranded significant volumes of the world's oil supply. The strait is a critical chokepoint for global energy shipments, and its disruption has created supply constraints that outweigh the modest output increase.

cards.headline: Nvidia signs AI infrastructure deals with South Korean tech companies including SK Group
cards.teaser: The chipmaker struck partnerships with major South Korean firms to advance artificial intelligence infrastructure and memory chip technology.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced deals with South Korean technology giants including SK Group to expand artificial intelligence infrastructure. The agreements include a multiyear technology partnership between Nvidia and SK Hynix to advance memory chips designed for AI applications, with Nvidia's new Vera chip set to use SK Hynix memory components.

South Korean internet company Naver said it will build gigawatt-scale AI factories using Nvidia technology. The partnerships position South Korean firms as key suppliers and partners in Nvidia's push to meet growing demand for AI computing infrastructure and specialized hardware.

cards.headline: Nvidia tops Wall Street Journal list of best companies for the future
cards.teaser: The chipmaker took the top spot in the 2026 ranking of companies considered best positioned for long-term success.
cards.body:
Nvidia claimed the top position in the Wall Street Journal's 2026 ranking of Best Companies for the Future. The list identifies firms best positioned to sustain success as business environments grow increasingly dynamic.

The Journal's methodology evaluates companies across multiple dimensions including their innovation capacity, competitive market position, and ability to adapt to future challenges. Nvidia's ranking reflects its dominant standing in the AI chip and infrastructure markets.

cards.headline: Marks and Spencer launches traineeship program for 1,000 young people
cards.teaser: The British retailer introduced a new scheme aimed at addressing the growing number of young people not in employment, education, or training.
cards.body:
Marks and Spencer has launched a traineeship program for 1,000 young people, targeting a persistent challenge in the labor market: youth disengagement from employment, education, and training. The initiative is designed to address this growing problem by providing practical support and opportunities.

The scheme equips participants with workplace skills and hands-on experience, helping them establish a foothold in the job market and move toward more stable employment pathways.

cards.headline: Netherlands achieves lowest youth unemployment rate through comprehensive education system
cards.teaser: The country maintains one of the world's lowest rates of young people not in education, employment, or training through policies that ensure no dead ends.
cards.body:
The Netherlands has achieved one of the world's lowest rates of young people aged 16 to 24 who are not in education, employment, or training. The country's success has drawn international attention as a model for addressing youth disengagement.

The Dutch approach emphasizes eliminating barriers that create long-term disconnection from the labor market. By designing pathways that allow young people to move seamlessly between education and work, the system prevents gaps that can lead to prolonged unemployment or withdrawal from the workforce.

hero.headline: Astronomers identify source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space
hero.body:
Astronomers have identified the source of mysterious radio signals that have puzzled scientists for two decades. The signals originate from a binary star system consisting of a white dwarf star accreting material from a companion star. The discovery was published in the journal Nature and has been described as a breakthrough in understanding these cosmic phenomena.

A student astronomer played a key role in pinpointing the location of these periodic radio emissions. The signals repeat in a predictable pattern, which had made them particularly intriguing to researchers trying to understand their origin. The system involves what scientists describe as a vampire star, a white dwarf that pulls material from its companion, creating the conditions that produce both radio and X-ray emissions.

The binary system generates both radio waves and X-rays as the white dwarf accretes matter from its partner star. This combination of emissions provided researchers with what they called a Rosetta stone for decoding the signals. The predictable nature of the emissions allowed astronomers to trace them back to their source after years of observation and analysis.

White dwarfs are the remnants of stars that have exhausted their nuclear fuel and collapsed to roughly the size of Earth while maintaining significant mass. When a white dwarf is part of a binary system, it can pull material from its companion through gravitational forces. This process, known as accretion, generates intense energy that can be detected across vast distances of space.

The identification of this source helps astronomers understand similar phenomena observed elsewhere in the universe. Repeating radio signals from space have sparked scientific interest and speculation about their origins. This discovery provides a natural explanation for at least one class of these signals and gives researchers new tools for identifying and studying similar systems throughout the galaxy.

cards.headline: Apple prepares second attempt at AI rollout at WWDC
cards.teaser: Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference begins with expectations for a Gemini-powered Siri and other AI features after previous stumbles.
cards.body:
Apple is holding its Worldwide Developers Conference with plans to unveil new AI features including a redesigned Siri powered by Gemini technology. The company is attempting a second rollout of AI capabilities after facing challenges over the past two years. The conference will showcase iOS 27, macOS 27, and other software updates.

The event represents an important moment for Apple as it works to compete in the AI space where other tech companies have moved more aggressively. Observers are watching to see whether Apple can deliver meaningful improvements to Siri and integrate AI capabilities across its product ecosystem. The keynote address is being streamed for developers and the public.

cards.headline: Nvidia announces RTX Spark chip as most efficient PC processor
cards.teaser: Nvidia unveiled the RTX Spark chip alongside new N1x and N1 laptop processors, positioning the technology as a competitor to Apple Silicon.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced its RTX Spark chip at Computex, describing it as the most efficient PC chip the company has built. The chip is part of a broader push by Nvidia and Microsoft to reinvent Windows PCs for what they call the age of personal AI. Nvidia also revealed specifications for its N1x and N1 laptop processors.

The RTX Spark chip is being compared to Apple Silicon in terms of efficiency and performance. Microsoft showcased its new Surface Laptop Ultra at the same event, demonstrating hardware that leverages Nvidia's new chip technology. The announcements signal a renewed effort to make Windows PCs competitive in performance and battery efficiency with Apple's laptop offerings.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE design revealed in early leak
cards.teaser: Images of Samsung's upcoming affordable flagship phone show a new design with an updated camera configuration.
cards.body:
Samsung's Galaxy S26 FE appeared in leaked hands-on images showing a redesigned phone with a modified camera bump. The affordable flagship model borrows design elements from Samsung's premium flagship line. The images circulated online ahead of any official announcement from the company.

The S26 FE represents Samsung's strategy of offering flagship features at a lower price point. The new camera bump design marks a visible departure from the Galaxy S25 FE. Samsung has not confirmed release timing or specifications for the device.

cards.headline: Gears of War: E-Day announced as Xbox console exclusive launching in October
cards.teaser: Microsoft revealed a new Gears of War game that will release only on Xbox Series X/S and PC, not on PlayStation 5.
cards.body:
Microsoft revealed Gears of War: E-Day at its Xbox Games Showcase, confirming it will launch in October exclusively on Xbox consoles and PC. The game will not release on PlayStation 5, despite earlier rumors suggesting a multiplatform release.

The exclusive announcement marks a shift in Microsoft's recent strategy, as the company had been moving toward releasing Xbox titles across multiple platforms. The October launch positions E-Day as a major release for the holiday season.

cards.headline: Persona 6 revealed at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: Atlus officially announced Persona 6 with a green color scheme and graveyard imagery, confirming earlier leaks were accurate.
cards.body:
Atlus officially announced Persona 6 at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 during Summer Game Fest. The confirmation came as a brief teaser, marking the long-awaited return of the beloved JRPG series.

The announcement generated excitement among fans who had been waiting for news about the next mainline entry. Beyond confirming the game's existence, Atlus revealed minimal additional details about the project.

cards.headline: Valheim sets September 9 release date for version 1.0
cards.teaser: The Viking survival game will exit early access after half a decade with a final release that includes the Deep North biome.
cards.body:
Iron Gate Studio announced that Valheim will exit early access and launch version 1.0 on September 9. The release concludes the game's nearly five-year early access period on PC and introduces the Deep North, the final planned biome. This frozen environment features new enemies and challenges described as ancient evils in a treacherous landscape.

The full 1.0 release marks the completion of the developers' original vision for the game, delivering all planned biomes and content. Valheim is also coming to Nintendo Switch 2 as part of the milestone launch.

hero.headline: Nelly Korda wins first U.S. Women's Open title by one shot
hero.body:
World number one Nelly Kord claimed her first U.S. Women's Open championship on Sunday, finishing one stroke ahead of England's Charley Hull at Riviera Country Club. The victory represents her fourth major championship and marks the achievement of a lifelong goal for the American golfer.

Kord secured the win with a steady final round, posting a two-under 69 to hold off both Hull and Gaby Lopez. The dramatic conclusion came on the 18th green, where her second putt from just over two feet caught the edge of the cup and curved around the circumference before dropping in. That final putt proved decisive in capturing the title.

This U.S. Women's Open win is Kord's second consecutive major victory, continuing a strong run of form at golf's biggest events. Her triumph at Riviera demonstrates her ability to perform under pressure when the stakes are highest. The championship adds one of golf's most prestigious titles to her growing collection of accomplishments.

Hull, who has established herself as one of England's leading golfers, came up just short in her pursuit of a first major championship. Despite solid play throughout the tournament, she could not overcome Kord's steady performance down the stretch. The narrow one-shot margin underscores the competitive level of women's professional golf at the major championship stage.

Kord's victory at Riviera Country Club highlights her all-around skills. The course is known for testing every aspect of a golfer's game, and her win there demonstrates her versatility and consistency. The $2.5 million first-prize check represents the financial reward for her triumph.

The win adds momentum to Kord's 2026 season and continues American dominance in women's golf on the global stage. Her status among the sport's elite players is further cemented by this major championship victory. Throughout the tournament, Kord's performance under pressure showcased why she maintains her world number one ranking.

Kord has been one of women's golf's most reliable performers at the highest level of competition. Her ability to close out tournaments and deliver when it matters most remains a defining characteristic of her game. With this U.S. Women's Open title secured, she adds another chapter to an already impressive career resume and fulfills a childhood dream of winning one of professional golf's most coveted trophies.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
cards.teaser: Alexander Zverev captured his first Grand Slam championship at the French Open, defeating Flavio Cobolli in the final.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title by winning the French Open, defeating Italy's Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in the final. The second seed's victory came in a five-set match that ended when Cobolli missed an overhead on the second championship point, prompting Zverev to collapse on his back in tears.

The win marks a breakthrough moment for Zverev after three previous Grand Slam final losses. Prior to this French Open victory, he had achieved success at Masters 1000 events, the ATP Finals twice, and earned Olympic gold in Tokyo 2020, but a major championship had eluded him until now.

cards.headline: Former Bulls champion Stacey King dies at 59
cards.teaser: Stacey King, who won three NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and later became a beloved broadcaster, has died at age 59.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bulls announced the death of Stacey King, a three-time NBA champion with the team during the franchise's dynasty years. King played alongside Michael Jordan and was part of championship teams before transitioning to a successful broadcasting career.

King became a popular television analyst for Bulls games, known for his enthusiastic commentary and deep knowledge of the team. He remained closely connected to the organization and the Chicago basketball community throughout his broadcasting career.

cards.headline: UNC baseball advances to College World Series with walk-off win
cards.teaser: North Carolina defeated USC 4-3 with a ninth-inning rally capped by Owen Hull's walk-off hit, earning a trip to Omaha.
cards.body:
Owen Hull hit a walk-off in the ninth inning to lift North Carolina past USC 4-3 in their Super Regional matchup. The Tar Heels scored the decisive run in the final frame to secure the victory.

The win eliminated USC and sent UNC to the College World Series in Omaha for the national championship tournament.

cards.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns delivers two-way impact in first NBA Finals
cards.teaser: Karl-Anthony Towns has excelled on both ends of the floor for the Knicks in the NBA Finals, particularly in defending Victor Wembanyama.
cards.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns has made a significant impact in his first NBA Finals appearance with the Knicks, contributing on both ends of the court. The center has proven effective defensively, including against Spurs star Victor Wembanyama.

After the Knicks won Game 2, Towns paid tribute to his late mother. His strong performance in the Finals has fueled conversations about how his play might influence the team's future roster moves and potential pursuit of additional stars.

cards.headline: Denny Hamlin wins at Michigan for third victory of 2026
cards.teaser: Denny Hamlin captured his third win of the season at Michigan International Speedway in a race marked by a major wreck and red flag.
cards.body:
Denny Hamlin won the FireKeepers Casino 400 at Michigan International Speedway, earning his third victory of the 2026 NASCAR season. Hamlin had earlier captured the pole position despite his car suffering damage during qualifying.

The race was halted by a red flag after a serious collision between Christopher Bell and Chase Elliott that damaged the track wall. Hamlin maintained his position through the stoppage and post-race inspection to secure the win.

cards.headline: Alabama baseball Super Regional game time pushed back
cards.teaser: Alabama's Super Regional matchup with St. John's has been moved to a later start time after weather delays suspended play.
cards.body:
Alabama baseball's Super Regional game against St. John's will resume at a later time after weather interrupted play. The Crimson Tide holds a commanding position, sitting six outs away from advancing to the College World Series in Omaha when rain forced a suspension.

Alabama won the first game of the series. The weather delay postponed the continuation of Game 2, which will determine whether the Crimson Tide advances or if the series extends further.

hero.headline: Death of a Salesman Dominates 2026 Tony Awards with Six Wins
hero.body:
Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman became the most awarded play revival in Tony Awards history, winning six awards at the 79th ceremony held at Radio City Music Hall and hosted by singer Pink.

The production claimed the award for best revival of a play. Director Joe Mantello praised Miller's work as a story that "still talks to us through time." Nathan Lane accepted on behalf of the cast, calling it a play that "continues to teach us who we are as humans and Americans." The six wins surpassed the previous record for a play revival, with the production having previously won for best play in 1949 and best revival in 1984, 1999 and 2012.

John Lithgow won best leading actor in a play for his role as Roald Dahl in the antisemitism drama Giant, making history at age 80 as the oldest man ever to win a competitive acting Tony. The previous record was held by Roy Dotrice, who won at 77 in 2000. This marked Lithgow's third Tony Award, coming 53 years after his first win. "It's an extraordinarily important play of this moment," he said on stage.

Lesley Manville took home the leading actress award for the Broadway transfer of Oedipus, defeating Rose Byrne and Carrie Coon. Making her Broadway debut, Manville said: "I'm a bit overwhelmed, it was my first time on Broadway so this is such a big deal."

Laurie Metcalf won best featured actress in a play for her role in Death of a Salesman, capturing her third Tony Award. She beat out June Squibb and Aya Cash for the honor.

Bess Wohl's Liberation was named best play after recently winning the Pulitzer Prize for drama. "This is the honour of a lifetime," Wohl said. It marked the first time a female playwright has won the award since 2009, making Wohl only the fourth woman to have won.

The musical Schmigadoon! won best musical, with producer Lorne Michaels noting: "Sometimes singing, dancing, a lot of jokes and a happy ending is really all you need." The show captured three additional awards.

Ragtime's new take on the classic musical won four Tonys, including best revival of a musical. Joshua Henry and Caissie Levy won for leading actor and leading actress respectively. This marked Henry's first win after four previous nominations. "Every artist in this room, every artist at home, fight, fight, fight to be heard," Henry said.

The Lost Boys, an adaptation of the 1980s vampire film, won four awards including featured actor and featured actress from a musical. Cats: The Jellicle Ball, a queer ballroom reinvention of Andrew Lloyd Webber's classic, won three awards including best direction of a musical.

Alden Ehrenreich won best featured actor in a play for his Broadway debut in a revival of the dating comedy Becky Shaw.

Pink opened the ceremony as Peter Pan, later leading a star-packed performance of her Moulin Rouge hit Lady Marmalade with guests including Lea Michele and Megan Thee Stallion.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Reboot Takes Top Box Office Spot with $55 Million Opening
cards.teaser: The new Scary Movie film defeated Masters of the Universe at the domestic box office, continuing a trend of low-budget comedy hits.
cards.body:
The sixth installment of the Scary Movie franchise claimed the weekend box office crown with a $55 million opening, according to industry reports. The R-rated comedy edged out Masters of the Universe, which opened in second place. The film continues the franchise's tradition of spoofing popular horror movies, though critical reception was mixed, with reviewers noting that successful jokes were sparse in this installment targeting films from Scream to Sinners.

The opening reflects a broader box office trend favoring lower-budget productions over bigger-budget competitors in recent weeks.

cards.headline: Dear You Extends China Box Office Dominance with $17 Million Weekend
cards.teaser: The family drama from Jinant Film TV held the top position for another weekend as Masters of the Universe opened in Chinese theaters.
cards.body:
Dear You secured RMB115.3 million, equivalent to $17 million, during the June 5-7 weekend in China, maintaining its lead at the country's box office. The film directed by Lan Hongchun and starring Li Sitong and Wang Yantong has now reached a cumulative total of $238.5 million since its release.

The low-budget cultural production from Jinant Film TV continued to outperform expectations and larger releases. Masters of the Universe debuted during the same weekend but failed to overtake the family drama's sustained performance. Dear You's extended run at the top represents one of the bigger domestic successes in the Chinese market this year.

cards.headline: The Vampire Lestat Premiere Shifts Series Narration Perspective
cards.teaser: The Interview With the Vampire spinoff series premiered with stars discussing how the show's narration differs from the original.
cards.body:
The Vampire Lestat premiered with cast members comparing the new show's narrative approach to the Louis-centered storytelling of Interview With the Vampire. The series enters what reviewers called a vibrant Vampire Lestat era for the franchise, shifting the perspective to the titular vampire character.

The premiere episode's opening scene generated immediate discussion among viewers and critics. Reviews described the already successful Interview With the Vampire franchise as entering a new phase with the spinoff. The premiere schedule launched the series on its planned run, adapting the Anne Rice novel series for television audiences.

cards.headline: Angelina Jolie Attends Son Knox's High School Graduation
cards.teaser: The actress appeared at her son's graduation ceremony ahead of his scheduled Muay Thai competition.
cards.body:
Angelina Jolie beamed with pride at her son Knox's high school graduation ceremony, celebrating the 18-year-old's completion of secondary school. The actress was present to mark this important academic milestone in Knox's life.

Following his graduation, Knox has a Muay Thai fight on the horizon. The teenager has been training in the martial art and will compete in what marks his first public match since finishing high school.

cards.headline: Luke Evans Attends Tony Awards with Partner Fran Tomas
cards.teaser: The Welsh actor and his partner wore coordinating outfits to the Broadway awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Luke Evans and partner Fran Tomas appeared together at the 2026 Tony Awards in matching red-themed looks. The couple coordinated their fashion choices for the Broadway ceremony held at Radio City Music Hall.

Evans currently stars in The Rocky Horror Show on Broadway. The actor wore a jockstrap, corset, and high heels during his stage performance at the ceremony. Evans recently sat for an interview discussing 24 hours in his life while performing in the production, and his fashion choices were featured in coverage of Adam Lippes Resort 2027 Fashion Show.

cards.headline: FCC Chairman Criticizes Scott Pelley Over 60 Minutes Firing Comments
cards.teaser: Brendan Carr called the veteran journalist out of touch for expressing surprise at losing his position on the news program.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, recently fired from CBS News, has accused the network's executives of interfering with his journalism. Pelley claimed that CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss pressured him to alter a segment about an immigration officer's killing of Minneapolis protester Renee Good, requesting changes that would align with a different narrative of events. In a public statement, Pelley alleged that network management instructed him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting and gave politicians influence over interviews.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr criticized Pelley on social media, characterizing him as out of touch for expressing surprise at his termination. Carr suggested that disconnect between established journalists and public perception contributes to declining trust in media institutions.

hero.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to strike Iran as tensions escalate
hero.body:
President Trump appealed to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from retaliating against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomatic efforts, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the conversation. The call came as the Israeli military confirmed it had struck targets inside Iran in response to an Iranian missile attack.

Trump told reporters before the call that he intended to ask Netanyahu not to respond to Iran's strike, which Tehran said was motivated by an earlier Israeli attack on Beirut. The exchange of strikes between the two nations risks escalating tensions across the entire Middle East region and could undermine ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran.

The Trump administration did not authorize the initial Israeli strike in Beirut, according to a senior U.S. official. Despite Trump's appeal for restraint, Israel proceeded with its retaliatory strikes on Iranian military targets. The sequence of events marks a significant escalation in the months-long conflict between Israel and Iran.

Trump's attempt to limit Israel's military response reflects his administration's broader strategy to prevent escalating Israel-Iran tensions from derailing diplomatic channels with Tehran. The president has focused on maintaining negotiations while managing regional conflicts and supporting American allies in the area.

When asked about whether the military actions contradicted his 2024 campaign promise of avoiding new wars, Trump dismissed the suggestion. He argued that his approach does not betray his "no new wars" message as he campaigned for the White House.

The confrontation between Israel and Iran has created significant diplomatic challenges for the administration. Saturday's emergency UN Security Council meeting grew contentious after Secretary General António Guterres condemned both the U.S.-Israeli strikes and Iran's retaliatory attacks as violations of international law.

The timing of events placed particular focus on the Trump administration's international engagement. The first lady presided over a UN Security Council meeting on Monday focused on children, technology, and education in conflict zones. Melania Trump emphasized education's role in preventing conflict and called for protecting children's access to learning. The session came just days after the escalated strikes between Israel and Iran.

Iran's UN ambassador criticized the timing as hypocritical, noting that Washington was convening a meeting on child protection while simultaneously launching airstrikes on Iranian cities. Iranian state media reported that strikes had killed at least 165 people at a girls' school in southern Iran, though the Israeli military said it was unaware of strikes in that area, and the U.S. military said it was investigating the reports.

The crisis has tested Trump's ability to balance multiple diplomatic objectives including supporting Israel, pursuing negotiations with Iran, and maintaining broader regional stability. The outcome of these efforts remains uncertain as both nations have demonstrated willingness to conduct military operations despite presidential appeals for restraint.

cards.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets for Gulf ally reconstruction
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect Iranian assets to help Gulf allies rebuild from war damage.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department is planning to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in the rebuilding process resulting from Iranian damage from the war. A source aware of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's thinking confirmed the plan to CBS News.

The move comes as the U.S. attempts to manage escalating tensions between Israel and Iran while supporting regional partners. The use of Iranian assets represents one tool in the administration's broader strategy to address the conflict's regional impact.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. She defeated her opponents to secure the party's nomination for the November general election.

If elected, Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She previously made history as one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress before joining the Biden administration.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges UFC fight planned for White House South Lawn
cards.teaser: A legal filing seeks to block a UFC event scheduled at the White House for President Trump's birthday.
cards.body:
A lawsuit has been filed to stop a UFC fight scheduled to take place on the White House South Lawn on June 14, President Trump's birthday. The legal challenge contends that the Trump administration's authorization of the event was unlawful.

The filing raises questions about the appropriateness of hosting a commercial sporting event on White House grounds. The lawsuit comes as the administration has pursued closer ties with UFC and its leadership.

cards.headline: Children's wellbeing declined nationally since pandemic
cards.teaser: A new report shows children in 29 states are faring worse than before the COVID pandemic.
cards.body:
Children's wellbeing has declined nationally from 2019 to 2024, with kids in 29 states experiencing worse conditions than before the COVID pandemic, according to a new report. Rising costs and reductions in safety-net programs have been identified as factors that could further strain families.

The decline in children's wellbeing has broader implications for the nation's future. Healthy, safe, fed, and educated children with strong family relationships are better positioned to thrive and become independent, contributing adults.

cards.headline: Bass and Raman advance to runoff in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass will face Councilmember Nithya Raman in November's general election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman are projected to face off in November's general election to lead the country's second largest city. With 87 percent of votes counted, Bass received 34.68 percent and Raman received 27.12 percent.

Raman gained ground in recent vote counting, pulling within two points of Republican candidate Spencer Pratt before ultimately securing second place. The November runoff will determine who leads Los Angeles for the next term.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead early returns in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republicans and Democrats are vying for their party's nominations to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading in early returns from California's gubernatorial primary. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing alongside Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton for their party's nominations.

The winner will replace Gov. Gavin Newsom, who is termed out of office. California's primary system allows the top two vote-getters to advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.
